working_set.verdict: 8 GiB held the serving workload and the whole database in RAM (OS page cache 6.7 GB, 5 GB available, no swap) with little headroom: the exact scans took about 1 s each, but one extra 1.7 GB process pushed them to about 16 s because the volume then served the reads at about 130 MB/s, and a heavy full-text phase evicted HNSW pages (dense p50 6.5 ms to about 300 ms). The 2 GB shared_buffers cannot hold the 1.3 GB HNSW index alongside everything else (74% buffer hit ratio on the first bench). Fine for this corpus on a dedicated box; not enough to run anything memory-hungry beside Postgres.
